chapter.heading: God’s Perfect Knowledge of ManFor the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David.
chapter.v:
O Lord,
You have searched me and known me. [Jer. 36:1 b 2 Kin. 24:1, 2; 2 Chr. 36:4- 6; Dan. 1:1,]

You know
my sitting down and my rising up;You understand my thought afar off.

You comprehend
my path and my lying down,And are acquainted with all my ways. [Jer. 1:2 d Jer.]

For there
is not a word on my tongue,But behold, O Lord, You know it altogether. [Jer. 7:13,]

You have
hedged me behind and before,And laid Your hand upon me. [2 Kin. 17:13; [Is. 55:6, 7]; Jer. 18:11; Ezek. 18:30; [Jon.]

Such knowledge
is too wonderful for me;It is high, I cannot attain it.

Where can
I go from Your Spirit?Or where can I flee from Your presence? [Deut. 32:21; Jer. 7:19; 32:30]

If I
ascend into heaven, You are there;If I make my bed in hell, behold, You are there.

If I
take the wings of the morning,And dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea, [Jer. 1:15 i Is. 45:1; Jer. 27:6 j Jer.]

Even there
Your hand shall lead me,And Your right hand shall hold me. [Is. 24:7-11; Jer. 7:34; 16:9; Ezek. 26:13; Hos. 2:11; Rev. 18:23 l Eccl.]

Indeed, the
darkness shall not hide from You,But the night shines as the day;The darkness and the light are both alike to You. [Is. 13:20; Jer. 50:3 (Ezra 1:1)] [2 Chr. 36:21, 22; Ezra 1:1; Jer. 29:10; Dan. 9:2]

For You
formed my inward parts;You covered me in my mother’s womb.

I will
praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made;Marvelous are Your works,And that my soul knows very well. [Jer. 50:9; 51:27, 28 q Jer. 51:27 r Jer. 27:7] [Jer. 50:29;]

My frame
was not hidden from You,When I was made in secret,And skillfully wrought in the lowest parts of the earth. [Job 21:20; Ps. 75:8; Is. 51:17; Rev.]

Your eyes
saw my substance, being yet unformed.And in Your book they all were written,The days fashioned for me,When as yet there were none of them. [Jer. 51:7; Ezek. 23:34; Nah.]

How precious
also are Your thoughts to me, O God!How great is the sum of them!

If I
should count them, they would be more in number than the sand;When I awake, I am still with You. [Jer. 25:9,]

Oh, that
You would slay the wicked, O God!Depart from me, therefore, you bloodthirsty men.

For they
speak against You wickedly;Your enemies take Your name in vain. [Job 1:1; Lam. 4:21 y Jer. 47:1-7; Ezek. 25:16,] [Is. 20:1]

Do I
not hate them, O Lord, who hate You?And do I not loathe those who rise up against You? [Jer. 49:7]

I hate
them with perfect hatred;I count them my enemies. [Jer. 47:4; Zech. 9:2-4 c Jer.]

And see
if there is any wicked way in me,And lead me in the way everlasting. [Jer. 25:20; 50:37; Ezek. 30:5]
